Selects the NVIDIA CUDA GPU backend.
Selects the Vulkan compute GPU backend.
Selects the browser WebGPU backend; f64 call sites fall back to the df32 (~48-bit) tier or CPU since WGSL has no native f64.
Selects ordinary host (CPU) memory for a GPU buffer allocation.
Selects pinned host memory for a GPU buffer allocation, for faster host-to-device transfer.
Selects device-only memory for a GPU buffer allocation.
Selects unified/shared memory for a GPU buffer allocation (Metal, or CUDA managed memory).
Requests no synchronization for a GPU buffer sync call.
Requests a host-to-device copy for a GPU buffer sync call.
Requests a device-to-host copy for a GPU buffer sync call.
Requests a full two-way sync for a GPU buffer sync call.

Multiplies two signed 128-bit values with wrapping two's-complement semantics.
Negates a signed 128-bit value with wrapping semantics.
Performs a logical right shift on a signed 128-bit bit pattern.
No-op fallback macro when the LLVM backend is disabled.
Returns the disabled-backend fallback value for shared-library exports.
Returns the TensorCore capability bits known to this adapter.
Returns the TensorCore capabilities available in the context.
Returns the backend bits compiled into TensorCore.
Returns the backend bits available at runtime.
Returns the TensorCore device-family code for a context.
Reports whether the device exposes unified memory.
Reports whether the device supports BF16 operations.
Reports whether the device supports int8 operations.
Reports whether the device supports TensorOps M5.
Returns the last TensorCore backend status code.
Widens a signed 64-bit integer to esk_i128 (sign-extending).
Widens an unsigned 64-bit integer to esk_i128 (zero-extending).
Constructs an esk_i128 from explicit high/low 64-bit limbs (little-endian limb order: hi:lo).
Converts an esk_i128 to its stable two-u64 FFI marshalling struct (esk_i128_abi, little-endian lo-then-hi).
Converts the stable two-u64 FFI marshalling struct (esk_i128_abi) back to an esk_i128.
Adds two esk_i128 values with wrapping two's-complement semantics.
Subtracts two esk_i128 values with wrapping two's-complement semantics.
Multiplies two esk_i128 values with wrapping two's-complement semantics.
Negates an esk_i128 value with wrapping two's-complement semantics.
Shifts an esk_i128 value left by s bits (0 <= s < 128); vacated low bits are zero-filled.
Shifts an esk_i128 value right by s bits, sign-preserving (arithmetic shift).
Shifts an esk_i128 value right by s bits, zero-filling the vacated high bits (logical shift).
Three-way compares two esk_i128 values; returns -1, 0, or +1.
Reports whether two esk_i128 values are bit-for-bit equal.
Adds two esk_i128 values, writes the wrapped two's-complement result to *out, and returns true if the mathematical sum overflowed 128 bits.
Subtracts two esk_i128 values, writes the wrapped two's-complement result to *out, and returns true if the mathematical difference overflowed 128 bits.
Multiplies two esk_i128 values, writes the wrapped two's-complement result to *out, and returns true if the mathematical product overflowed 128 bits.
Computes the exact 128-bit product of two signed 64-bit integers; a product of this width never overflows.
The maximum representable esk_i128 value, 2^127 - 1.
The minimum representable esk_i128 value, -2^127.
Formats an esk_i128 as a NUL-terminated base-10 string into a caller buffer (needs >= 41 bytes); returns the number of characters written (excluding the NUL), or -1 if the buffer is too small.
Parses a base-10 signed integer literal into an esk_i128; returns true on success and sets *overflow to true if the literal does not fit in 128 bits.
Rounding mode: truncate the fractional bits toward zero.
Rounding mode: round to nearest, ties to even.
Rounding mode: round up with probability equal to the fractional part, using the caller-supplied esk_rng stream.
Overflow policy: wrap the out-of-range result into the W-bit range with two's-complement wraparound.
Overflow policy: clamp the out-of-range result to the [min, max] bounds of the W-bit range.
Seeds an esk_rng stream (SplitMix64) used for stochastic rounding; reproducible for a given seed.
Advances an esk_rng stream and returns its next 64-bit output.
Constructs a fixed<W,F> value from a raw integer, masking/checking it against the W-bit range.
Returns the minimum representable raw value for a W-bit fixed-point range, -2^(W-1).
Returns the maximum representable raw value for a W-bit fixed-point range, 2^(W-1) - 1.
Adds two fixed<W,F> values of matching (W,F) exactly, applying the given overflow policy; reports overflow through the optional out-parameter.
Subtracts two fixed<W,F> values of matching (W,F) exactly, applying the given overflow policy; reports overflow through the optional out-parameter.
Negates a fixed<W,F> value, applying the given overflow policy; reports overflow through the optional out-parameter.
Multiplies two fixed<W,F> values of matching (W,F) via an exact widened product, then rounds per the given rounding mode and narrows under the given overflow policy.
Divides one fixed<W,F> value by another of matching (W,F), rounding per the given mode and narrowing under the given overflow policy; returns false (result untouched) on division by zero.
Constructs a fixed<W,F> value from a signed 64-bit integer under the given overflow policy; reports exactness through the optional out-parameter.
Converts a fixed<W,F> value to a signed 64-bit integer, truncating the fractional part toward zero; reports exactness through the optional out-parameter.
Constructs a fixed<W,F> value from a double under the given rounding mode and overflow policy; reports exactness through the optional out-parameter.
Converts a fixed-point value to double and reports exactness when requested.
Constructs a fixed-point value from a float with explicit rounding and overflow policy.
Converts a fixed-point value to float and reports exactness when requested.
Requantizes a fixed<W,F> value to a different (W,F) under the given rounding mode and overflow policy; reports exactness through the optional out-parameter.
Formats a fixed<W,F> value as an exact decimal string (it is always a dyadic rational) into a caller buffer; returns characters written (excluding the NUL), or -1 if the buffer is too small.
Resets an esk_accum128 running sum and its element count to zero.
Adds an int64 value to an exact 128-bit accumulation and advances its count.
Adds an int128 value to an exact 128-bit accumulation and advances its count.
Combines a partial esk_accum128 accumulator into another, summing both the running total and the element count.
Returns the current running-sum value held by an esk_accum128 accumulator.

Computes the block-scaled dot product of two int8 vectors (scale_a * scale_b * sum(a[i]*b[i])) as fixed<128,F>; the integer accumulation step is exact and order-independent. Reports exactness of the final scaling through the optional out-parameter.

Computes the block-scaled dot product of two int16 vectors (scale_a * scale_b * sum(a[i]*b[i])) as fixed<128,F>; the integer accumulation step is exact and order-independent. Reports exactness of the final scaling through the optional out-parameter.
Computes the raw integer dot product sum(a[i]*b[i]) of two int8 vectors in esk_i128, with no scaling; exact and order-independent.
Computes the raw integer dot product sum(a[i]*b[i]) of two int16 vectors in esk_i128, with no scaling; exact and order-independent.
Computes the raw integer dot product sum(a[i]*b[i]) of two int32 vectors in esk_i128, with no scaling; exact and order-independent.

Computes a row-major exact integer matrix product A[rows,inner] x B[inner,cols] into out, with every cell the two-u64 ABI form of an exact i128 sum; returns false without touching out if a required pointer is NULL or a size/index product would overflow size_t, and treats inner==0 as a valid all-zero no-op.
